title: Lesson 6: Close Read-aloud, Culminating Task: What Makes Day and Night
objective: Students will understand what causes day and night on earth by closely reading an informational text, participate in a structured science discussion using evidence from notes, and describe observations about the sky through independent and shared writing.

what_is_taught.skill: identify and discuss prepositions in a poem
listen to and echo a poem with gestures
answer a focus question about day and night using text details
create a diagram to represent day and night on earth
participate in a structured small-group science discussion using notes as evidence
use sentence starters to build on peers' ideas during discussion
listen actively and show understanding during peer discussion
write independently to describe observations using adjectives
engage in shared writing to describe the position of the moon using prepositions
use classroom resources to support writing (word walls, high-frequency word lists, letter-sound charts)

what_is_NOT_taught: complex vocabulary instruction beyond basic science terms

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify prepositions and details in text and images
student_actions.oral_production: echo poem verses, participate in science talk using sentence starters, share ideas orally
student_actions.written_production: write descriptions independently and contribute to shared writing
student_actions.procedural_application: apply science talk protocol steps in triads
student_actions.investigation_handson: create diagrams representing day and night
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain ideas during science talk and describe observations
student_actions.comprehension_response: answer focus questions about day and night using text and notes evidence, respond to prompts about moon position and poem content

evidence.quote: Tell students that you will read the poem first on your own as they listen, then they should echo each verse as you read it a second time. Remind students of the gestures and hand motions that they created in the previous lesson.
What word(s) describe where we see the sun, moon, and stars in these verses?' (above and below)
Circle and/or highlight the prepositions in each verse as you continue to read the poem aloud. Refer to 'Where Are They? The Sun, Moon, and Stars' poem (example, for teacher reference) as necessary.
If time permits, invite students to read the poem with you one last time.
Review the focus question by reading it aloud.
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
Tell students that today they will create a diagram that shows day and night on earth.

During the culminating task, support fine motor skills and expression of knowledge by providing a scaffolded diagram. (Example: Offer pre-cut labels and shapes and/ or include a line to denote the halves of the earth.) (MMR, MMAE)
Invite students to move safely to a spot on the edge of the whole group meeting area.
Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner:
Invite a few students to share out.
Ask two student volunteers to help you model how to build onto a group member's idea:
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
Guide students through each step of the Science Talk protocol using the question:
Circulate to observe students as they discuss. Gather data on using the Speaking and Listening Checklist. Prompt students with questions to help them expand on their ideas.
Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner:
I can record my observations from images/videos of the sky in my Sky Notebook.
Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner:

Display page 4 of the Sky notebook and follow the same process established in Lesson 5 by reading the prompt aloud, encouraging students to use pictures and words to show their thinking, and reminding them to use the Adjectives anchor chart for their descriptions.

Circulate and support students as necessary. Encourage them to use classroom resources (Word Walls, high-frequency word lists, and alphabet or letter sound combination charts). Refer to Sky notebook (answers, for teacher reference) as necessary.
Refocus students whole group.
Display the Describing the Position of the Moon recording form and using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group.
Tell students that they will have the opportunity to describe the location of the moon in the picture through shared writing.

As students share responses, use their ideas to answer the prompt. Begin by circling one of the pictures that most closely resembles the location of the moon in the photograph and then model writing a complete sentence to describe the location of the moon. (Example: 'The moon is behind the branch.')
If productive, cue students with a challenge:

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model reading the poem aloud with gestures; model circling and highlighting prepositions; model creating a diagram of day and night; model using sentence starters during Science Talk; model writing complete sentences describing moon position.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What word(s) describe where we see the sun, moon, and stars in these verses?
What makes day and night on earth?
What does this learning target mean?
How will you show your partner you are listening to him or her?
What is one thing you did well during your Science Talk triad?
Where do we see the moon?
What if the moon was above the branch? How would that change the picture?

scope.breadth: poem comprehension, informational text comprehension, science discussion, writing about observations
scope.depth: identifying prepositions, answering focus questions, diagram creation, structured discussion, independent and shared writing

sections_covered.warm_up: Engaging the Learner: 'Where Are They? The Sun, Moon, and Stars' Poem
sections_covered.direct_instruction: Close Read-aloud Culminating Task: What Makes Day and Night, Entire Text
sections_covered.check_for_understanding: Shared Writing: Describing the Position of the Moon

supports.english_language_learners: Use of sentence frames, grouping by language proficiency, use of Prepositions Construction board, and encouragement to ask for repetition or slower speech.
supports.universal_design_udl: Use of gestures, scaffolded diagrams, pre-cut labels, and supportive writing tools such as pencil grips and slanted desks.
supports.below_level_reinforce: Provide pre-cut labels and shapes for diagram; model sentence frames and use of prepositions.
supports.above_level_extend: Encourage students to add details during Science Talk and challenge with hypothetical questions about moon position.

assessment.method: Observation of student participation in Science Talk, review of diagrams and writing in Sky notebooks, and shared writing contributions.
assessment.recognition_vs_production: Both recognition of text details and production of oral and written responses.
